articles.title: DOL Finalizes New PBM Transparency Rules for Employer Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new transparency regulations governing pharmacy benefit managers, requiring rapid compliance from health plans. These rules impose stricter reporting requirements on self-funded employers regarding PBM pricing, fees, and contract terms under ERISA. Plan sponsors must quickly audit their PBM arrangements to ensure compliance with the heightened disclosure mandates.

articles.title: DOL Finalizes PBM Fee Disclosure Rule for Health Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new fee disclosure rules targeting pharmacy benefit managers and plan service providers. This regulation requires greater transparency around indirect and direct compensation, directly impacting self-funded employers by giving them more visibility into PBM pricing structures and administrative fees. Plan sponsors must review these disclosures to fulfill their fiduciary duties under ERISA.

articles.title: DOL Finalizes Sweeping PBM Transparency and Disclosure Rule for Employer Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized a sweeping new rule requiring PBMs to disclose comprehensive pricing, fee, and compensation data to self-funded employer health plans. This regulation significantly strengthens fiduciary oversight for plan sponsors, enabling employers to better audit PBM contracts and evaluate hidden costs like spread pricing. The rule increases accountability across the supply chain, giving self-funded employers unprecedented visibility into their pharmacy benefit expenditures.
articles.source_line: Source: Healthcare Dive; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:42:19 GMT

articles.title: DOL Finalizes New Transparency Rule for Pharmacy Benefit Managers
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized a new transparency rule targeting pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) operating in employer-sponsored health plans. This regulation increases reporting requirements for PBMs, allowing self-funded employers greater visibility into pricing, rebates, and fees. The rule reinforces fiduciary oversight obligations for plan sponsors managing prescription drug benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: Fierce Healthcare; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:54:51 GMT

articles.title: DOL Rule Imposes New Transparency Mandates on PBMs and Employers
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has introduced new rules increasing transparency requirements for pharmacy benefit managers and self-funded employer health plans. This regulation heightens reporting obligations regarding broker and PBM compensation, empowering plan sponsors to better scrutinize benefit costs and contract terms.
articles.source_line: Source: Modern Healthcare News; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:37:00 GMT

articles.title: DOL Issues Final PBM Fee Disclosure Rule for Self-Funded Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has released a final rule requiring pharmacy benefit managers to disclose direct and indirect compensation to self-funded employer health plan sponsors. This regulation enforces stricter transparency standards under ERISA, empowering plan fiduciaries to better evaluate PBM pricing and hidden fees. Self-funded employers will now have enhanced visibility into spread pricing and administrative costs to fulfill their fiduciary duties.

articles.title: Six Companies Sue UnitedHealth for ERISA Fiduciary Breaches in Benefit Plans
articles.summary: Six companies have filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth, alleging breaches of fiduciary duty under ERISA regarding employee benefit plans. This legal action highlights growing employer scrutiny over plan management and fiduciary responsibilities, which directly impacts self-funded health plan sponsors. Such litigation signals increased legal risk and accountability for major PBMs and health plan administrators.

articles.title: DOL Finalizes New PBM Fee Disclosure Rules for Self-Funded Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new regulations regarding transparency and fee disclosures for pharmacy benefit managers operating in employer-sponsored health plans. This rule directly impacts self-funded employers by increasing visibility into PBM compensation structures, indirect compensation, and administrative fees. Plan sponsors will need to review their current contracts and reporting mechanisms to ensure compliance with these enhanced disclosure mandates.
articles.source_line: Source: American Hospital Association; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 20:21:47 GMT

articles.title: The GLP-1 Dilemma: Balancing Breakthrough Innovations With Employer Financial Realities
articles.summary: This article examines the intense cost pressures and strategic challenges self-funded employers face when covering high-demand GLP-1 medications. It underscores the urgent need for robust utilization management and benefit design strategies to handle rising specialty drug expenditures.
articles.source_line: Source: Penn LDI; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:37:29 GMT

articles.title: The Rising Cost of GLP-1 Coverage for Employers
articles.summary: The surging demand for GLP-1 weight-loss medications is forcing self-funded employers to grapple with unsustainable drug benefit costs and difficult coverage decisions. Plan sponsors are increasingly seeking strategic utilization management solutions to balance employee demand with long-term financial viability.

articles.title: Eli Lilly Raises Revenue Outlook on Surging Weight-Loss Drug Demand
articles.summary: Eli Lilly has upgraded its full-year revenue projections driven by massive, continued demand for its GLP-1 weight-loss medications. This persistent market growth underscores the mounting financial pressure self-funded employers face as they navigate complex coverage decisions and escalating plan costs for obesity therapies.

articles.title: DOL Final PBM Rule Impacts Employer Formularies and Rebate Management
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has released a final rule regarding PBM practices that directly affects how self-funded employer health plans manage drug rebates and formulary design. This regulatory shift requires plan sponsors to closely examine their PBM contracts, fiduciary responsibilities, and transparency standards to ensure compliance. The ruling adds new complexity to how self-funded employers capture pharmacy savings and structure their benefit plans.
articles.source_line: Source: Pharmaceutical Commerce; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 19:38:43 GMT

articles.title: Trump's Labor Department Pushes PBM Transparency for Employer Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor is increasing regulatory pressure on PBMs to disclose pricing methodologies and rebate data to self-funded employer health plans under ERISA fiduciary rules. This move empowers employers to better audit their pharmacy benefits and combat hidden costs.
articles.source_line: Source: PJ Media; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 22:32:00 GMT

articles.title: 340B Contract Pharmacy Case Restokes Program Intent Scrutiny
articles.summary: A recent legal case involving 340B contract pharmacies has renewed debate over the program's original intent and operational scope. This scrutiny impacts drug pricing dynamics and regulatory oversight relevant to PBMs and self-funded employer health plans managing specialty drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: Targeted Oncology; Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:05:54 GMT

articles.title: IQVIA Quantifies Financial Impact of 340B and Maximum Fair Price Duplicate Discounts
articles.summary: New research from IQVIA evaluates the financial overlap and scale of 340B drug pricing and Maximum Fair Price (MFP) duplicate discounts. Understanding these pricing intersections is critical for self-funded employers and PBMs monitoring drug cost drivers and program integrity.
